story:
Marquis Sabonach is the smallest peer on the Roll, no bigger than an imp, and he built half the court. He is a mason. In the Uncounted Age the halls of the hollow were caves, holes in the rock with whatever throne their lord had made of its last kill, and Sabonach, a demon of High Lord Oro's household, began cutting them into halls: pillars, arches, stairs, the long gallery of the approach that Adremal later cut his Rolls into. He shaped Oro's hall first, and then, for payment, the halls of the other high lords, and then the chapter house of the Chthonic Knights and the cloisters of the Inquisition. Every arch in the hollow that has not fallen is his.

He was not always small. The court says each hall he finished took something out of him, that a mason who shapes stone with his own body puts himself into it, and that by the First Roll he had put so much of himself into the halls of the court that what was left would fit on a duke's palm. He did not stop. He has kept building every Roll since, smaller each time.

In the Tenth Roll Field Marshal Nebir came to him with the one commission he had never been asked for. The Marshal wanted a keep: a keep of the court's own, cut from the rock under the frontier, so that the doors would answer to the court as they answer to the realms. Sabonach drew it. The drawing is in his rooms beside Oro's hall, a keep with towers and a gate and a lord's room, the size of a fingernail. He took it to the Chancellor, who told him the Roll has no line for a keep. Sabonach has started building it anyway, a stone at a time, somewhere he will not say.
legend: Sabonach is tiny (a fraction of the size of the other marquises) and stands outside High Lord Oro's hall in the north-east with Duke Sallis and Earl Mercur. Do not let the size fool you: level 73, full marquis health, no script. Kill him after Sallis and Mercur and before you go near Oro and his clones. Players say he is hard to click on in a big fight and easy to lose under a tank, so assist the main assist. Some swear he is building a demon keep somewhere in the dungeon and that one day the doors will open for the demons. That is a story, but it is a good one.

loremasterTopic.text: The mason of the court, of High Lord [Oro]'s household, who cut the caves of the hollow into halls and grew smaller with every one. For Field Marshal [Nebir] he has drawn a keep of the court's own, and is building it, though the Roll has no line for one.

bookPage: From a Midgard runemaster's account: The little demon sat on a block of stone outside the three high lords' hall, cutting a smaller block with a chisel no longer than my thumbnail. I watched him for some time before he noticed me. On the block beside him was a drawing scratched into the stone: a keep, with four towers and a gatehouse and a lord's room, all of it smaller than my palm. I am a runemaster and I know a plan when I see one. It was not a sketch. It was a mason's plan, measured and true, for something meant to be built full size.
